d2m1-cov.lead: Every policy answers **two questions**: whose is it, and what does it pay? The Payer-First Principle then decides which payer each Medical Bill goes to first.

concepts.text: Third-party is the at-fault driver's coverage; first-party answers to the client's side: **who you claim against** changes
Only coverage that pays the claim stacks: BI, then the UM/UIM layers. **Bills and the car** stay outside
MedPay and PIP pay accident Medical Bills **regardless of fault**, fast, while liability is still disputed
more: MedPay: reasonable accident Medical Bills up to its limit, never wages
PIP, where a state requires it: also a share of lost wages and replacement services
This file: **$5,000 Harbor Point PIP** on the Escape John Doe rode in
Verify PIP on every file; never assume it

concepts.text: UM/UIM follows the person: an occupant reaches the vehicle's policy, **a resident relative the household's**
more: Host UM: John Doe was an occupant of Kevin Alvarez's 2020 Ford Escape
Relative UM: he is a resident relative of Margaret Doe, insured by Cardinal State
Bluewater adds nothing: **UM rejected in writing** on 03/14/2024
Together the two UM layers reach $30,000

concepts.text: Some policies credit what MedPay or PIP paid against what they owe: **verify the form in writing**
A payer with subrogation claims its payments back from the recovery; without it, **what it paid stays paid**
An in-network provider takes the plan's rate and writes off the rest: **no balance billing**, a smaller lien
more: Crescent Pain & Spine billed $3,400.00; Peach State paid $1,860.00
The $1,540.00 difference is written off for good
Peach State's reimbursement claim starts from **what it paid**, never what was billed

concepts.text: Medicare pays only after no-fault and liability coverage, and **recovers by statute**; report the case to the BCRC

d2m1-l1.lead: Claim set-up is coverage determination: finding **which policies apply** and what limits and exclusions they carry. The LOR puts the firm on each one.

concepts.text: The firm's formal notice that it represents the client: **it moves all contact** off the client and onto the firm

The insured differs: Robert Smith (Keystone), Kevin Alvarez (Harbor Point), Margaret Doe (Cardinal State)
States he was injured, a Demand Package will follow, all contact goes to the firm
Requests limits, additional coverage, every Declaration Page and preservation
Atty. Thorne signs; you send by the preferred method and log delivery

concepts.text: Four questions: is coverage valid, what type applies, what are the limits, any exclusions? **Every LOR request** chases an answer
Who is legally responsible, and how far: **clear, shared or disputed**. Atty. Thorne weighs it; you secure the proof
Third-party: the other driver's carrier, adverse to the client. First-party: policies covering him. **Each letter differs accordingly**
The adverse carrier learns only what it must: **anything you give it** can be used against the client

Never his phone, address, date of birth or employer
First-party carriers, Harbor Point and Cardinal State, may verify his details
Nothing more than needed: anything written now is quoted back later

more: All three stack carriers noticed on 02/17/2026
UM policies carry notice conditions: **late notice hands a defense** to the carrier
No UM letter asks for payment before the BI tender is documented

concepts.text: Asks the carrier to keep photos, statements, video, the vehicle and its event data: **liability proof that can vanish**
The carrier's written receipt of the LOR, sometimes stating coverage and limit: **the first written answer** you log
more: Expected within 24–48 hours of the LOR
None by the **third business day**: follow up
On this file: letters out 02/17/2026, follow-up dated 02/20/2026
Keystone may hold written limits until a written request with authorizations Atty. Thorne approves

d2m1-l2.lead: Coverage verification turns a reported fact into **a confirmed one in writing**: every limit, form and exclusion traced to the document that proves it.

concepts.text: One row per carrier, the file's single coverage record: **status, source and date** show what is proven
Reported, noticed, acknowledged, disclosed, confirmed in writing: **only the last is proof**; each earlier status is a lead

more: Named insured and policy number
A policy period that covers 02/06/2026
The insured vehicle and its VIN: the one in the collision
Coverages, limits, deductibles, listed or excluded drivers, endorsements
Keystone's, dated 03/20/2026: **BI $10,000 per person**

Harbor Point confirmed 03/02/2026: add-on (excess), no PIP non-duplication
Had it been reduced: $20,000 − $10,000 = $10,000 Host UM, a $30,000 stack
Whether a form applies is Atty. Thorne's call; you record it

concepts.text: Only liability and UM layers stack; PIP, PD and collision coverage are **separate benefits, tracked apart**
A policy's exclusions matter as much as its limits: **a verified zero** is a fact, an assumed one a guess
A stalled carrier is a bottleneck: find the root cause, act now, then **prevent the next occurrence**

d2m2-l1.lead: Once the claim is set up, the Case Plan runs on **three pillars**: clinical care, functional status and subrogation management, which sets who pays.

concepts.text: The default sequence: MedPay or PIP first, health insurance next, an LOP last. **Order keeps liens down**
First-party coverage for Medical Bills regardless of fault, up to its limit; **unlike PIP, no wages**
more: John Doe's PIP: **$5,000 at Harbor Point**, as a passenger in the Escape
$640.00 left after the 03/27/2026 visit
Reaches $5,000.00 on the 06/12/2026 MMI visit: nothing left

concepts.text: Pays covered care at its contract rate, but may hold **a reimbursement right** against the recovery
The client's signed agreement that a provider is paid from any recovery: **a consensual lien** on his net
more: Only for care earlier payers can't carry: Riverton Spine & Rehab is out of network
Summit Imaging's 03/11/2026 request declined: **PIP pays first**
Terms, template and signature are Atty. Thorne's; you prepare, route and transmit
Never promise a provider an amount, a reduction or a date

concepts.text: The usual route of care: emergency, imaging, chiropractic and PT, orthopedics, pain management, surgery. **Each stop needs a payer**
Evaluating clinical and functional outcomes, not checking boxes: **ask about the plan**, not just “How are you?”
more: Facilitation: transport, paperwork, scheduling
Coordination: every provider on one plan
Advocacy: step in when care is denied or stalls
End each contact: **what might get in the way** of treatment this week?

concepts.text: Stepping in when care is denied or stalled by bureaucracy: **adjust the plan** to the immediate issue first
Combined opioid, muscle relaxant and sedative, or rising doses without a new diagnosis: **raise it with the provider**

d2m2-eob.lead: Every payer reports what it did with a bill: the Health Plan in an **Explanation of Benefits**, PIP in its payment history. Read both before any lien.

concepts.text: The plan's account of one processed claim: **not a bill**, but proof of who paid what
Billed is the provider's charge; allowed is the plan's fee schedule. **The gap is written off** in network
Short codes that explain each line: CO-45 is the fee-schedule write-off, AC1 **flags a possible accident**
more: CO-45: charge above the in-network fee schedule; the difference is the provider's
AC1: possibly accident-related, which attaches the plan's reimbursement right
AC1 also brings the plan's accident questionnaire
Route it to Atty. Thorne **before John Doe returns it**

concepts.text: The deductible, copay and coinsurance left to the patient: **the most a provider may bill** in network
Billing the patient for a contractual write-off: **not allowed in network**, so an error, not a lien
more: Crescent's 07/01/2026 statement asks John Doe for $1,540.00: **the write-off**
File it beside the EOB
Route it to Atty. Thorne the same day
Draft the written request that Crescent correct its account
Tell John Doe what you're doing and when he'll hear back
Whether he owes anything is Atty. Thorne's call

concepts.text: The carrier's ledger of every PIP check: date of service, amount paid and **the limit remaining**
Once PIP's limit is spent, later bills come back unpaid: **route them to the next payer**
more: Harbor Point's five checks: $685.00, $640.00 three times, $2,395.00
Later bills come back with a notice of exhaustion
The firm's PIP Log (RS71) tracks each check and the limit remaining
Pitfall: sending a bill to PIP after exhaustion

concepts.text: Matching every provider balance to each payer's EOB or check, so **no paid bill becomes a lien**

d2m2-l2.lead: Mastering **the Standard Treatment Map** separates a Case Manager who observes a recovery from one who drives it; deviations trigger denials and IMEs.

concepts.text: Days 1–14: ER, imaging, initial PT, documenting causation. Weeks 2–8: active PT, specialists, **measuring functional gains**
Weeks 9–24: injections, work hardening, **barriers to return to work**. Then home exercise and as-needed visits
The provider's finding that further care won't improve the condition: **it closes the treatment phase** and opens pre-demand
When a client drifts off the map, identify why first: **clinical, psychosocial or systemic**, before funding stops
more: Clinical: a new complication
Psychosocial: yellow flags like fear-avoidance or catastrophizing, or no transport to therapy
Systemic: an authorization or referral delay
This file: visits missed from 04/03/2026 for want of transport, **a psychosocial variance**

concepts.text: The immediate action for any red flag: Assess the danger, Coordinate the fix, Track it. **Documentation supplies counsel's why**
more: Climb one documented rung at a time
Rung 1, clinical: the provider's office manager
Rung 2, administrative: written notice to the carrier causing it, copied to Atty. Thorne
Rung 3, legal: **Atty. Thorne's call**, such as an LOP
Write each step as a GIRP note: Goal, Intervention, Response, Plan

concepts.text: The utilization-review test: common for the mechanism of injury, and **objective functional gain**, not subjective pain alone
Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound: goals **defensible to clinicians and adjusters** alike, like the week-6 measures
more: Week 6: 20–30% more range of motion or a lower pain score
No disability-index change by week 12: **a plateau**; ask the provider about a specialist

concepts.text: Clinical, legal and financial loops, with you as the router: **one broken loop** can stall a case for months

d2m3-l1.lead: The Golden Rule: coordinate, don't commingle. The medical plan and the legal claim are **two parallel tracks** that never cross-contaminate, even in a gap interview.

concepts.text: Legal opinions in medical or call notes let the defense **impeach your neutrality**; record facts, never conclusions
Under A-C-T, a gap in care is **a legal danger**, not medical: it routes to Atty. Thorne
more: After each reason, ask **what shows it in writing**
A work schedule, a doctor's availability note, a travel log, a text or a receipt
Open a dated task for each document
Record his explanation in his words, beside its document; no view on value

concepts.text: Reflect and paraphrase his words, then summarize: he **feels heard and corrects** what you got wrong
more: Funnel: **broad open questions first**, then follow-ups on his own words
Closed questions last, only to pin a date, a name or a document
One question at a time; let pauses run
Never lead: a question that names a reason gets agreement, not information

concepts.text: Confidential firm-client communication is privileged; **a third person** in the conversation can put that protection at risk
more: Record only with consent: date, who is on the call, **his spoken yes**
Confirm he can talk privately
Ask Atty. Thorne before anyone joins
Label the recording privileged
Keystone asks for a Recorded Statement: he declines and refers it to the firm

steps.label: Assess
steps.text: Medical danger (fever, hardware failure) → the provider today; legal danger (gaps, generic notes) → Atty. Thorne

steps.label: Coordinate
steps.text: Clarify with the provider's office, then remove the barrier the client names: transport, scheduling, referrals

steps.label: Track

steps.label: Back to monitoring

framework.note: For a gap in care, Assess is already answered: a legal danger, routed to Atty. Thorne

d2m3-l2.lead: Case Managers must understand **the why behind the paperwork**: continuity is proved by what the record already shows, never by what it is asked to say.

concepts.text: An unbroken path along the Standard Treatment Map, each step following from the last: **the chain an adjuster tests**
Any break in care, before first treatment or midstream. Adjusters read it as **minor, healed or unrelated**
Written by EMS, providers and employers as events happened: **strongest proof**, since nobody wrote them for the claim
more: EMS Run Report: neck stiffness, 02/06/2026
Urgent-care note, 02/20/2026: onset at the collision
Northgate call-outs, 02/09–02/13
The 02/07/2026 Riverton Drug receipt
The full text thread to Margaret Doe, **not chosen screenshots**

concepts.text: Each provider's history repeats mechanism, onset and body region; **agreement across charts** is what makes continuity credible
more: Mechanism: the collision
Body region: neck and right arm; the earlier chiropractic visits were low back
A conflict goes to Atty. Thorne that day: **never resolve it yourself**

concepts.text: A treating doctor's opinion linking injury to collision: **the bridge across a gap**, requested by Atty. Thorne
more: You assemble the records for his request letter and track the reply
You **never draft or suggest** its words

concepts.text: A record changes only by its author's dated addendum: altering one **can be evidence tampering** or fraud
A work note proves only what its author saw or ordered at a visit: **unexamined days need other proof**
more: Check the signer and the visit date
Check that the days covered follow from that visit
02/09–02/13, before any exam: **Northgate's Attendance Record** is the proof
Never request a note written to order

d2m4-l1.lead: A full pre-demand audit is **the final stress test**: the move from collecting information to using it, leaving the defense zero easy outs.

concepts.text: Narrative, physicality and medicals **must all agree**; if one is out of line, the case value collapses
The provider's finding that care has reached its plateau: **the incurred Specials are complete**, and the audit can begin
Medical Bills + lost wages + Property Damage: the provable dollar loss. **Every line needs a document**

Lost wages: 9 shifts × 8 h × $22.00 = $1,584.00, verified by Northgate
Audited BI Specials: $16,401.40
Out-of-pocket costs from the trip log and their receipts
The Civic runs on its own Keystone PD claim, outside the $40,000
Future care stays out of the audited total

concepts.text: Three passes: chronology for gaps, coding for duplicates, prior history for pre-existing conditions. **Find weak spots first**
more: Chronology: the 14 days and the 19-day disruption, each with its documented reason
Coding: duplicate or unbundled lines
Prior history, 5–10 years back: low-back chiropractic visits, resolved; **no prior neck complaint**
Every line: fits the mechanism, clinically ordered, backed by objective findings

concepts.text: Health Plans, government payers and LOP providers may claim repayment from the recovery: **every lien shrinks the net**
more: Peach State: $1,860.00, funding type recorded
Consensual: the LOP, $6,105.00
PIP: no reimbursement right against John Doe (03/02/2026)
Ask Harbor Point in writing whether it reserves PIP subrogation against Robert Smith
**$7,965.00 in liens** behind a $10,000 BI limit

concepts.text: Photos of the point of impact, estimate against final bill, supplements: **PD proves the force** behind the injury
Read the file as the adjuster will: social media, a minor-impact (MIST) label, venue. **Name each value killer**
Verified limits in the order they open: what each policy can pay, **not the claim's worth**

Facts next, audited and sourced
Risks, each paired with the document that answers it
Decisions needed, as questions only Atty. Thorne can answer
Options with their operational consequences; decisions recorded the same day, in his words

The defense-eye audit looks for what shrinks a claim: social media, a MIST label, venue. **Counsel weighs each one**

Disruption → the A-C-T record

A MIST label → **the structural supplement** answers it

steps.text: Do the facts match the physical evidence: photos, the Police Report, the scene?

steps.label: Valuation
steps.text: Are damages calculated accurately: bills, wages and future care, each justified by a document?

steps.label: Risk Assessment
steps.text: Weak spots the defense will argue: comparative negligence, social media, a MIST label, venue

d2m2-lop.lead: A **Letter of Protection** keeps care going when no payer will: the firm promises the provider payment from the settlement.

concepts.text: The firm's written promise to pay a provider's bill from the settlement: **a claim against the recovery**, not insurance
more: Signed before the first visit, and filed
Riverton Spine & Rehab's: signed 02/23/2026, Financial class LOP / attorney
The client **still owes the balance**
What it means for his recovery is Atty. Thorne's to explain

concepts.text: Health insurance, MedPay and PIP are checked first; the LOP is **the last resort**, and the reason is recorded
Grows with every visit; the itemized ledger every 30 days keeps **the Liens tab and the Net Sheet** current
Options and logistics only: a list, network status, the booking. **The client chooses**; any firm relationship is disclosed
more: A list of providers who accept an LOP or the client's plan
Each with location, hours and network status
Book the appointment **he chooses**
Never recommend one provider, promise a result, or say care helps the case
Log who was offered, who he chose and why, in his words

d2m2-cost.lead: Treatment costs the client money no provider bill shows: **documented when it happens**, it can reach the demand.

concepts.text: Mileage, rides, parking, prescriptions, co-pays, equipment and any rental the owner paid: **each with its receipt**
more: Mileage to and from every treatment visit
Rides and parking when the client has no car
Prescriptions, co-pays and deductibles
Medical equipment: a brace, a cervical pillow, a TENS unit
A rental the owner paid: days past the cutoff, or a rate above the cap

concepts.text: Date, provider and round-trip miles for every visit, **kept from the first appointment**
more: One line per visit: the date, the provider and the round-trip miles
Kept as treatment happens, never rebuilt from memory at the demand
Mileage is claimed at the rate the governing state's rules allow; Atty. Thorne confirms it
For reference, the IRS rates when this course was written: **20.5¢ a mile medical**, 72.5¢ business

concepts.text: A rental the carrier didn't pay is **the owner's out-of-pocket cost**: receipt filed, routed with the PD claim
more: Days past the carrier's cutoff
A daily rate above the authorized cap
An upgrade's difference over a comparable vehicle
Keep the rental company's receipt and route it to Atty. Thorne

concepts.text: Each cost entered in **the Specials ledger** the day its receipt arrives; counsel decides what is claimed

d2m2-pip.lead: PIP pays regardless of fault, so a BI settlement must account for it: **where PIP is spent**, how fast, and whether it is credited or repaid.

concepts.text: The law prevents double recovery: Gross Settlement Value − PIP Paid = **Defendant's Remaining Liability**, where set-off applies
more: On a typical file: $60,000 − $10,000 PIP paid = $50,000 left for the defendant
Riverton is add-on: PIP **does not reduce BI or UM**
Harbor Point, 03/02/2026: no reimbursement right, no PIP non-duplication reduction
Whether a set-off is argued is Atty. Thorne's call

concepts.text: BI adjusters read PIP as **a severity signal**: a limit spent in days on ER bills reads as serious
In EMC states, PIP without an Emergency Medical Condition finding is **capped lower**, for example $2,500 of $10,000
more: The finding is the treating physician's clinical judgment
Check the first treating records for it **early in treatment**
No finding: more bills fall to the Health Plan, LOPs and the BI settlement
John Doe's Harbor Point PIP has no EMC ceiling

concepts.text: PIP spent on **non-negotiable hard costs** first; LOP providers reduce at the end more readily than hospitals
